items.question: What is Form W-8 (W-8BEN & W-8BEN-E) and what is its purpose?
items.answer: Form W-8 is a document required by the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for foreign individuals and business entities receiving income from US sources. It formally certifies non-US tax residency status, preventing default withholding tax of up to 30% from being withheld at the source on your compensation.

items.question: Is FormW8 affiliated with the US government, IRS, or contractor platforms?
items.answer: No. FormW8 is an independent and 100% free community project created to help users navigate complex US tax forms. We have no affiliation with the IRS, tax authorities, or platforms (such as Deel, Rippling, Upwork, or Remote). Users are solely responsible for the accuracy and completeness of their submissions.

items.question: Where can I find the official IRS forms and instructions?
items.answer: Official forms and detailed instructions are published directly on the official IRS.gov portal: [Form W-8BEN (Individuals)](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-8-ben), [Instructions for Form W-8BEN](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw8ben), [Form W-8BEN-E (Entities)](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-8-ben-e), and [Instructions for Form W-8BEN-E](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw8bene).

items.question: What is the difference between Form W-8BEN and Form W-8BEN-E?
items.answer: Form W-8BEN is intended for Individuals (freelancers contracting via individual tax ID) — check our [W-8BEN Guide for Individuals](/w8ben-pessoa-fisica). Form W-8BEN-E is exclusively for Legal Entities (corporations, LLCs, and incorporated businesses) — check our [W-8BEN-E Guide for Entities](/w8bene-pessoa-juridica).

items.question: Why do platforms like Deel, Rippling, Remote, Upwork, and Husky require Form W-8?
items.answer: US-based companies and contractor platforms are mandated by US federal tax law (Internal Revenue Code) to collect and maintain certified W-8 forms for all non-US contractors prior to disbursing funds. Without a valid W-8 on file, platforms are legally required to withhold 30% of your gross earnings. See our platform guides: [Deel](/plataformas/deel), [Rippling](/plataformas/rippling), [Upwork](/plataformas/upwork), and [Remote](/plataformas/remote).

items.question: What should I enter for Foreign Tax Identifying Number (FTIN)?
items.answer: For Brazilian contractors, your Foreign TIN is your national tax identification number: your CPF (for individuals on W-8BEN) or your company CNPJ (for entities on W-8BEN-E). You do not need to apply for a US tax ID (such as an ITIN or EIN) to provide remote international services.

items.question: How should Brazilian companies (SLU/LTDA) classify Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 on W-8BEN-E?
items.answer: For service-providing companies (software development, design, consulting, translation, marketing), standard IRS classification is 'Corporation' on Line 4 (Chapter 3) and 'Active NFFE' (Active Non-Financial Foreign Entity) on Line 5 (Chapter 4 FATCA), because gross income is derived primarily from active business operations rather than passive investments. See details in the [W-8BEN-E Entity Guide](/w8bene-pessoa-juridica).

items.question: What should I enter for permanent residence address on Form W-8?
items.answer: Enter your full permanent home address (for individuals) or your registered company headquarters in Brazil (for legal entities). The IRS strictly disallows P.O. Boxes, forwarding addresses, or 'in-care-of' addresses. FormW8 automatically sanitizes all accents into clean ASCII to prevent rejection.

items.question: Does Brazil have a double taxation treaty with the US? How does 0% withholding work?
items.answer: Brazil does not have a comprehensive double tax treaty for services with the US. However, services performed entirely from Brazil for US clients are legally categorized as 'Foreign Source Income', qualifying for 0% US withholding tax at the source under the Internal Revenue Code.

items.question: How long is a completed W-8 form valid?
items.answer: A signed Form W-8 is valid starting from the year signed through December 31st of the third consecutive calendar year (roughly 3 full calendar years). If any key information changes (such as company name, permanent address, entity type, or tax residency), a new form must be generated immediately.

items.question: How should I sign and submit the filled W-8 form?
items.answer: You can sign the generated PDF digitally via tools such as Adobe Acrobat, DocuSign, Apple Preview, or directly within your onboarding platform (such as [Deel](/plataformas/deel), [Rippling](/plataformas/rippling), or [Remote](/plataformas/remote)), or alternatively print, wet-sign, and scan. The date must strictly follow the US format month-day-year (MM-DD-YYYY).

items.question: Why can't names and addresses contain special characters or accents (á, ç, õ)?
items.answer: IRS processing systems and US compliance databases strictly adhere to standard 7-bit ASCII encoding. Accented characters or special symbols (such as ç, ã, é, º, ª) can cause data corruption or rejection in IRS systems. FormW8 automatically sanitizes all inputs into standardized ASCII without losing information.

items.question: Does FormW8 store my personal or tax data on servers?
items.answer: No. FormW8 is built on a 100% client-side, Zero-Data architecture. We never store any form data: no server receives your name, CPF, CNPJ or address. We only keep anonymous usage counters (for example, how many people reached the last step), with no cookies and no way to identify anyone. All PDF generation and ASCII sanitization happen strictly in your browser memory. Only when you choose to input a CNPJ or ZIP code, your browser queries public Brazilian open directories (ViaCEP, BrasilAPI, Minha Receita) to autocomplete your address. 100% manual, offline filling is always available.

items.question: Why was my payment on Deel, Rippling, or Upwork withheld at 30%?
items.answer: US tax legislation (Internal Revenue Code Chapter 3) mandates US payers to enforce a default 30% backup withholding tax if an international contractor does not provide a certified Form W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E. Once your valid form is verified by the platform, withholding is set to 0% for services performed outside the United States. Check our setup guides for [Deel](/plataformas/deel), [Rippling](/plataformas/rippling), [Upwork](/plataformas/upwork), and [Remote.com](/plataformas/remote).

items.question: How do I complete the US tax form for Google AdSense and YouTube?
items.answer: In your Google AdSense or YouTube Studio dashboard, navigate to Payments > Manage tax info. Select your account type (Individual for W-8BEN or Legal Entity for W-8BEN-E), confirm non-US residency, enter your Foreign TIN (national tax ID), and certify 0% withholding for digital services and content creation performed abroad. Follow the step-by-step walkthrough in our [Google AdSense & YouTube Guide](/plataformas/google-adsense).

items.question: How do I fill out Form W-8 for Apple Developer and Stripe Express?
items.answer: In App Store Connect (Agreements, Tax, and Banking) and Stripe Express, a certified W-8 is required before funds can be disbursed. Individual developers complete W-8BEN using their personal tax ID; incorporated businesses submit W-8BEN-E with 'Corporation' (Chapter 3) and 'Active NFFE' (Chapter 4 FATCA) using exact matching legal addresses. See our [Apple Developer Guide](/plataformas/apple-developer), [GitHub Sponsors Guide](/plataformas/github-sponsors), and [Stripe & Paddle Guide](/plataformas/stripe).

items.question: How do indie game developers complete the W-8 on Steam Direct and Epic Games?
items.answer: When onboarding a game on Steamworks (Valve) or the Epic Games Store, you will be prompted through the IRS tax interview. Select W-8BEN (for solo developers) or W-8BEN-E (for studios/companies). Entering your native Foreign Tax ID ensures exemption from 30% default withholding on global sales and royalties. See our [Steam Direct Developer Guide](/plataformas/steam).

items.question: Can solo entities, LLCs, or micro-businesses fill out Form W-8BEN-E?
items.answer: Yes. Any legally registered entity outside the US with a corporate tax identifier (such as Brazilian SLU, LTDA, MEI, or foreign LLC equivalents) is eligible for Form W-8BEN-E. Classify entity type as 'Corporation' under Chapter 3 and 'Active NFFE' under Chapter 4 FATCA. Learn more in the [W-8BEN-E Entity Guide](/w8bene-pessoa-juridica).

items.question: What should I do if my W-8 form is rejected by a platform?
items.answer: The 3 most common rejection reasons are: (1) Accented or non-ASCII characters in names or street addresses (automatically fixed by FormW8 ASCII sanitizer); (2) Date formatted as DD/MM/YYYY instead of US standard MM-DD-YYYY; (3) Mismatch between legal name on tax form and bank account beneficiary. Verify these three fields, re-generate on FormW8, and re-upload.

items.question: Why does ChatGPT recommend 'Disregarded Entity' and Deel rejects it?
items.answer: ChatGPT frequently translates 'single-member company' (such as Brazilian SLU or solo entity) literally to the US term 'Disregarded Entity' (Single-Member LLC). Under IRS classification rules, foreign limited entities are treated as autonomous corporate bodies and must be classified as 'Corporation' under Line 4 (Chapter 3) and 'Active NFFE' under Line 5 (Chapter 4 FATCA). Checking Disregarded Entity triggers a request for a US SSN/ITIN and leads to compliance rejection on platforms like Deel and Rippling.

items.question: How does tax optimization (Fator R) work for remote tech contractors in Brazil?
items.answer: Brazilian software engineers and designers operating via a corporate entity (Simples Nacional) can leverage 'Fator R' by maintaining a payroll/pró-labore of 28% or more of gross revenue. This reduces their Brazilian effective tax rate from ~15.5% (Annex V) to ~6% (Annex III). Combined with constitutional exemptions on PIS, COFINS, and ISS on service exports, contractors save thousands of dollars annually.

items.question: What should be filled in 'Special rates and conditions' (Part III of W-8BEN-E or Part II of W-8BEN)?
items.answer: For international contractors and developers performing services entirely outside the US, Part III (W-8BEN-E) and Part II (W-8BEN) can be left blank. Because the work is physically executed in Brazil or another foreign territory, the income constitutes non-US 'Foreign Source Income' and is exempt from US federal tax withholding by IRS statutory definition.

items.question: I live outside Brazil or I don't have a CPF. Can I use FormW8?
items.answer: Not yet. FormW8 is built for people who live in Brazil and have a CPF (or CNPJ): it is the foreign tax number on the form and the address must be Brazilian. If you are a foreign national living in Brazil, use the "I'm not Brazilian" link in step 3 to enter your country of citizenship. People who live in another country need different fields (their country's tax number and treaty benefits), which are not supported yet. US citizens do not use the W-8BEN: the correct form is the W-9.
